title: SqlPlanV1
description: A SQL statement that has passed the guard and is cleared for execution, together with everything the guard proved about it. Nothing executes without one of these; the executor takes a plan, never a raw string.

sql.description: The exact statement to execute, after LIMIT injection or clamping. This is what the UI's SQL panel shows — never the pre-guard generation.

dialect.description: SQL dialect the statement was parsed and rewritten for

tables.description: Every table the statement references, as resolved from the AST. The guard proves this is a subset of the retrieved schema subset; a table outside it is a bug or an injection.

limit_injected.description: True when the guard added a LIMIT the generation did not have

limit_clamped.description: True when the generation had a LIMIT larger than the cap and the guard lowered it

limit_value.description: The row limit in force on the statement

statement_timeout_ms.description: Timeout the driver enforces on this statement. The runtime enforces a separate wall-clock cap; both must be set.

schema_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the database schema the plan was built against. The semantic cache is scoped by this; a plan is never reused across a fingerprint change.
